note: HAND-WRITTEN. This file is the independent oracle for the similar-content rename matcher and
it was written BEFORE the matcher existed. It is never generated by running Nerve, and no
script writes it — scripts/make_history_fixtures.sh builds the repository, this file says what
the answer is. If it were produced by the thing it grades, the precision measurement over it
would be Nerve agreeing with itself, which is the exact failure a measured gate exists to
Every numerator/denominator below was computed by hand from the line contents the generator
writes, and fixtures/history-similar/README.md restates the arithmetic per commit so a reviewer
can check it without running anything. Commits are identified by the summary string the
generator commits, not by object id: an id could only be obtained by running the generator, and
keying on one would make this file a derived artifact.

verdicts.rename: the added path is the deleted path's content, moved and edited. Ground truth by construction: the generator wrote one file from the other.
verdicts.not_rename: two unrelated files that happen to share text — boilerplate, a licence header, a generated lockfile preamble, or nothing at all. Admitting one of these is a false positive and the gate is zero of them.
verdicts.unmeasurable: the pair cannot be measured at all: too few lines for a ratio to mean anything, or binary content that has no lines. Neither a positive nor a negative — an unanswered question, and it is excluded from precision and from recall rather than counted as a miss.

commits.label: c0
commits.summary: root commit: every file that is later deleted
commits.why: a root commit adds everything and deletes nothing, so there is no candidate pair. It still gets an analysis row: zero rows because there was nothing to pair is a different fact from zero rows because a bound refused.

commits.label: c11
commits.summary: c11: copy copy/original.txt to copy/duplicate.txt, leaving the original in place
commits.why: a copy leaves its source in the tree, so there is no deletion and therefore no candidate. The 19-of-20 shared lines are never measured, because a move has to be evidenced by a deletion as well as an addition.

commits.label: c12
commits.summary: c12: replace gen/old.lock with gen/new.lock, sharing ten lines

commits.label: c13
commits.summary: c13: move empty/a.txt to empty/b.txt, both empty
commits.why: two empty files are one blob oid, so this pair belongs to the exact-content matcher and the similarity matcher skips it. Emitting it under both evidence values would be the blend the plan forbids.

similar_content_pairs.why: a real move with twelve of twenty lines rewritten. 8 * 8 = 64 < 140, so the threshold misses it. This is the honest cost of a gate set for zero false positives, and it is published as a false negative rather than bought back by lowering the threshold.
two unrelated service definitions sharing fourteen lines of scaffold. 14 * 8 = 112 < 140. This is one of the two pairs that decide the threshold.

two unrelated documents sharing a sixteen-line licence header. 16 * 8 = 128 < 140. This is the pair that sets the threshold: at 4/5 it would be admitted (16 * 5 = 80 >= 4 * 20 = 80) and the false-positive count would stop being zero.
one deleted file, two added files that each keep eighteen of its lines. Both pairings are recorded and neither is promoted.
fan/merged.txt lines 1-18 are fan/left.txt's first eighteen lines.
fan/merged.txt lines 3-20 are fan/right.txt's first eighteen lines.

the same twenty lines in reverse order. A multiset cannot see order, so this measures whole. Documented rather than patched: the two blobs really do differ, and the method really does not distinguish them.
two lines each, beneath the three-line floor. A ratio over two lines is dominated by whether the file has a shebang.
both blobs contain a NUL byte, so they have no lines and a line ratio over them would be a number without a meaning.
two generated lockfiles sharing a ten-line preamble. 10 * 8 = 80 < 140.

exact_content_pairs.why: two empty files are the same blob oid, so this is the exact matcher's row and carries no measurement at all. The similarity matcher must not also emit it.
